//Executive summary

In Year 2, HP helped 1,492,030 young people in 220+ countries and territories start their AI learning journey, 149% of the 1 million target. HP also put laptops in the hands of 130 top learners.

HP did more than fund a course. It gave young people the skills (AI Fundamentals and partner AI courses), the tools (HP laptops as challenge prizes) and a stage (youth stories at UNGA, in the World Economic Forum journal and across global media). Winners are now using their HP devices to run businesses, teach classes, build apps and lead climate action in their communities.

//About the program

The AI to Opportunity Program is Goodwall’s flagship digital skilling initiative, delivered with HP as a founding partner of the NextGen AI Alliance. Year 2 of the partnership ran from 1 November 2025 to 31 October 2026 and was designed to scale AI literacy, practical AI skills and access to technology for young people worldwide.

At the heart of the program is AI Fundamentals, a mobile-first learning path co-created by HP, Microsoft and Cognizant that takes young people from AI curiosity to demonstrated, credentialed AI skills. Learners watch short, creator-led lessons featuring HP devices, put AI tools into practice through hands-on challenges, and return to the Goodwall app to show what they have learned. The strongest challenge entries win HP laptops, so top learners leave with the tools to keep building.

AI Fundamentals is the main entry point into a wider set of AI to Opportunity learning paths co-designed with NextGen AI Alliance partners.

//The partnership

HP is a founding partner of the NextGen AI Alliance, launched in 2025 by HP, Microsoft and Cognizant and powered by Goodwall. The Alliance brings public and private partners together to build AI-era skills for young people at scale.

Year 1 · HP Level Up

A digital inclusion program with six virtual challenges paired with HP LIFE courses. It accelerated 911,887 young people, trained 123,000+, generated 147M impressions and rewarded top learners with HP devices and cash.

Year 2 · AI to Opportunity

HP moved into a co-branded, founding-partner model. HP, Microsoft and Cognizant launched AI Fundamentals, the first shared AI curriculum of its kind, and HP technology became the reward that helps learners turn new AI skills into real-world outcomes.

Program objectives

1

Reach 1 million young people

Bring young people into AI learning (Youth Accelerated / Engaged).

2

Build credentialed AI skills

Demonstrated, assessed AI skills through AI Fundamentals and the wider AI to Opportunity program.

3

Put HP technology in young hands

Award laptops to high-potential youth and show what they do with them.

4

Position HP as the leader

Make HP the corporate leader for youth, AI skills and the future of work through stories, media and global convenings.

Top 10 countries · Youth Accelerated (to 2 Nov 2026)

The top 10 make up 79% of reach.

India became the largest market

Reach grew from 56,264 in April to 327,787 by early November, helped by the Gujarati and Telugu launch in July. India alone is 22% of all youth reached.

New markets broke through

Egypt (142,454) and Brazil (39,640) joined the top 10 in the second half of the year. Latin America and the Caribbean together reached about 121,000 youth, led by Brazil, Argentina (16,810) and Bolivia (11,881).

Africa stayed central

Nigeria, Egypt, Kenya and South Africa are all in the top 10, with Ghana (35,838) and Algeria (27,221) close behind.

Broad reach beyond the top 10

56 countries had 1,000+ youth accelerated, and 18 had 10,000+.

KPI definitions

Youth Accelerated / Engaged
Unique users who start their AI learning journey by (a) installing the Goodwall app via app store featuring of the NextGen AI Alliance or AI programming, plus organic installs and referral campaigns, or (b) engaging with AI Alliance programming content on Goodwall. Counted once if they do both.
Youth Trained
Unique users who started a course, watched educational videos, joined challenges or completed quizzes.
Youth Credentialed
Unique users who earned a badge, certificate or certification through an assessed demonstration of learning.
// 03 · Learning & challenges

AI Fundamentals

AI Fundamentals is the co-branded AI course HP built with Microsoft and Cognizant, and the most-used path in the AI to Opportunity program. Every lesson is presented by Gen Z creators and features HP devices.

Learners watch a short creator-led video, try a real AI tool, then come back to Goodwall to prove what they learned through a quiz or a practical challenge. Each module earns a badge; finishing the three core modules earns the AI Fundamentals certificate. The free in-app Goodwall AI Companion guides learners throughout.

Learning journey — AI Fundamentals modules

The learning path is made up of six modules. The first three are core modules; completing all three earns the full AI Fundamentals credential. The final three are bonus modules that let motivated learners go deeper.

// 04 · Youth & HP technology

The youth who won HP laptops

In Year 2, young people across the world earned HP laptops for their challenge entries. For many, it was their first reliable device. Skills got them in the door; the HP technology let them act on those skills every day.

What young people are doing with their HP technology

Laptop winners use their devices in five main ways: running a business, teaching others, studying for a career, acting on climate and creating content.

Entrepreneurship

Write business plans, run production, serve clients and market products.

Teaching and education

Build learning tools, prepare lessons and run workshops.

Healthcare and sciences

Turn complex lessons into study notes, prepare for clinical work and manage health data.

Climate and agriculture

Build farmer tools, research policy and advocate for climate action.

Creativity and content

Design, edit video, create digital art and run campaigns.

More HP laptop winners from the year

HP laptops went to the top entries in each monthly challenge round. These winners show the range of what young people are learning, building and solving with AI.

From AI-Curious to AI-Confident

AI Fundamentals drew an AI-aware, AI-curious audience. Most learners had already tried an AI tool and arrived with some confidence. The course turned that curiosity into structured skill they could show.

UNGA Week spotlight

22 September · Roundtable

AI to Opportunity Roundtable

35 leaders from tech, industry, philanthropy and the UN system met to answer one question: how can industry work together to build AI-ready nations? Guests included EY, Microsoft Elevate, Accenture, Deloitte, LinkedIn, SAP, GitHub, Cognizant, Micron, S&P Global, Generation Unlimited and Misk Global.

  • Michele Malejki opened the first theme, Building AI-ready workforce systems, drawing on HP's Future of Work Accelerator.
  • Ina Progonati spoke on Scaling collective impact: what each partner must bring for partnerships to work at scale.
  • HP OmniBook X Flip laptops played HP youth stories and program demos at arrival and during networking.
23 September · Dinner

100M Futures Dinner

The first 100 Million Futures Dinner launched a shared goal to connect 100 million young people to skills and economic opportunity by 2030. Senior leaders from Fortune 500 companies, government, philanthropy and academia asked how learning turns into earning in an AI economy.

  • Michele Malejki addressed the room on the future of work and where leaders should invest to build learning-to-earning pathways.
  • HP laptops ran “With HP I can…” reels, youth stories and impact videos across the venue.

What came out of the week

  • Both events were oversubscribed, and HP framed the conversation at both.
  • HP and Goodwall published a co-authored article in the World Economic Forum journal.
  • HP took part in Goodwall Studios, with interviews of Michele and Ina filmed for HP content.
  • Youth insights shared in the room: 42% of 22,000 Goodwall youth surveyed want to build their own venture; by 2030, 1.2 billion young people will enter the job market against roughly 400 million new jobs.

// 07 · Summary and looking ahead

Year 2 in summary

In Year 2, the HP-sponsored AI Fundamentals pathway accelerated 1,492,030 young people, 233,407 earned HP-branded credentials, and 130 HP laptops went to challenge winners. This section sums up what worked and what we would improve in Year 3.

What worked

Skills plus tools

Learners built AI skills on Goodwall, and HP technology rewards let winners put those skills to work every day in study, work and business.

Localization grew reach

The Brazil, India and Latin America launches helped Youth Accelerated more than double in the second half of the year.

Learners left more confident

Learners who felt very confident using AI rose from 64.4% to 77.9%, and more than half gave the course a perfect 10.

Young people think more of HP

Opinion of HP rose from 4.00 to 4.39 out of 5, and 91% would recommend HP after the course. INNOVATION was their top word for HP.

Stories gave HP a stage

Winner stories and youth insights from the program fed the newswire, Business Insider, the WEF op-ed and the UNGA showcases, giving HP leaders real proof to talk about.

HP was in the room

HP leaders spoke at both flagship UNGA Week events, and HP devices played youth stories at every in-person event Goodwall hosted.

What we would improve in Year 3

What we saw in Year 2What to improve in Year 3
Learners and Career Compass responses asked for practical, career-focused AI skills.Refresh AI Fundamentals with applied AI challenges, and integrate HP LIFE so learners can move on to deeper HP courses and credentials.
Winner stories drove the strongest engagement, but only one compilation video was produced.Plan stories into the calendar: regular “With HP I can…” stories, compilations for each flagship event, and a lasting home on the Goodwall website.
Every laptop winner was a potential story, and gathering photos and updates after delivery took extra follow-up.Build story capture into the prize process: collect photos, video and a short update from each winner when the laptop arrives.
The WEF op-ed and UNGA events gave HP leaders a global stage.Plan HP leadership moments earlier, with op-eds and speaking roles mapped to Davos, AI for Good and UNGA.
Youth surveys showed clear brand lift for HP after the course.Share regular youth insight reports with HP shaping the questions, to feed HP's own reporting such as the HP Futures report.
HP asked for meaningful ways for employees to take part.Open mentoring and volunteering for HP employees, such as an “Ask a Mentor” challenge and HP and Goodwall Youth Days. This will require Goodwall to have 501(c)(3) status or equivalent.
Closing

As a founding partner of the NextGen AI Alliance, HP gave young people more than a course. It gave them the skills, the tools and the stage to build their futures with AI. From a teacher in Kenya who now runs a tech NGO to a nursing student in the Philippines who found her voice, HP laptop winners show what becomes possible when learning comes with the technology to act on it.
